{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjccM8AAAABZkWz3g", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IfzhDK974", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3If", "number": 79, "title": "Correct V30MZ indirect CALL/JMP timing and destination alignment", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `d068ada04ccb96552f865eee7a23e8948365fc88`, `crates/ws-core/src/cpu.rs:806–828` uses residual charges of four/six clocks for indirect near/far CALL and JMP, without destination parity. This undercounts indirect dispatch and subroutine execution, advancing shared devices too little.

`cpu/jmp_tests.rs:461–498` preserves eight/eleven clocks for near/far memory JMP to odd target `1041`; the corrected serialized expectations are nine/fourteen.

## Expected outcome

Correct the six valid forms: near register/memory CALL, far memory CALL, near register/memory JMP and far memory JMP. Include necessary CPU, regression, fixture-consumer and documentation work.

Keep this milestone bounded to indirect timing. Return timing, full prefetch, effective-address hazards and unrelated bus policies remain separate gaps.

## Context

The clean local checkout matches inspected remote `main`. The open Issue/PR collection is empty; all 78 closed titles were checked. [Issue #77](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/issues/77) and [PR #78](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/pull/78) explicitly defer indirect control flow.

The [NEC V30MZ manual](https://www.renesas.com/en/document/lbr/v30mztm-hardware-preliminary), Appendix A, printed pp. 73/76, specifies decoded JMP register/memory-near/far-memory costs of **4/5/10**, and corresponding CALL costs of **5/6/12**, plus one clock for an odd destination. These assume completed decoding, aligned words, no waits/holds and qualified effective addressing. Subtracting normal operand/stack transfers already charged by this repository gives inferred residuals **4 for near forms, 8 for far forms**. Add actual fetch, pointer-read and stack-write costs, including existing alignment/waits, exactly once.

Correction record: the old AI-authored assumption treated current indirect costs as preservation requirements. Replace it with the accounting above and corrected nine/fourteen-clock examples. The manual and inspected transfer accounting justify this correction; architectural and regression acceptance remain required. Record further evidence-based corrections with the old assumption, replacement, source and rationale, without adding approval gates.

These are serialized emulator expectations, not complete console pipeline measurements. The inspected [WSTimingTest report](https://github.com/FluBBaOfWard/WSTimingTest/blob/025e606fc3b6615160ffdae485d992ffcad0c024/README.md) warns that aggregate results include pipeline/harness effects; its opcode-pattern workaround is unsuitable.

[Saved #77 validation](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/d068ada04ccb96552f865eee7a23e8948365fc88/docs/issue-77-validation.md) reports 265 workspace tests and complete production Chromium suites passing. Tests and consumers are present; this investigation ran no application builds or tests. Published #78 reviews and discussion are empty; criterion-level review appears in the saved report.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Record independent literal timing/state vectors before changing charges. Correct all six forms using actual transfers plus residual and destination parity. Replace obsolete expectations and current documentation; expected values must not call production timing helpers.
- [ ] Cover even/odd opcode, destination, pointer and stack addresses; register operands including SP; representative ModR/M addressing and displacement forms; segment overrides; instruction/pointer/stack offset wrapping and 20-bit/bank boundaries. Assert exact CS/IP/SP, full FLAGS, other registers/segments, return bytes and unrelated memory. Preserve near operand sampling and far CALL’s existing stack-before-pointer-read ordering, including overlapping pointers; calculate parity from the destination actually loaded. Exercise actual RET/RETF continuation without changing their timing policy.
- [ ] Cover internal RAM, mapped ROM pointer/fetches, mapped SRAM pointers/stacks, live A0 `00/04/08/0C` and existing SRAM waits. Retain transfer consolidation, SS stack selection, segment/BUSLOCK prefixes through seven prefixes, REP rejection and invalid far-register diagnostics. Exact access counts must detect unintended destination reads or duplicate transfers.
- [ ] Exercise emulated Mono/Color/SwanCrystal model configurations: Mono `00`; Color and SwanCrystal `00/80/C0/E0`, including live transitions back to `00`. Through normal `Machine::run_frame`, verify representative indirect CALL/JMP frame-boundary clocks, raster/frame progression, timer decrement and stereo-sample production, preventing an extra destination instruction. Preserve IRQ/TF priority, shadows, saved destination continuations, IRET/return integrity, REP/HALT and separate GDMA/SDMA reservations with existing capability/mode gates.
- [ ] Add an original, source-included CC0 cartridge through existing fixture tooling, with independent native and production Chromium consumers covering all six forms and even/odd destinations. Require absolute budgets, CPU-written execution/destination counts, CALL stack/return integrity, continuation markers, supported model/mode passes, stale-save invalidation and two fresh boots. Document every measured instruction, harness cost and timer quantization, identifying retained approximate costs. Demonstrate separately that old near-parity and far-charge behavior fails both consumers; record final corrected passes with matching fixture identities.
- [ ] Audit affected existing timing intervals and independently recalculate necessary budgets without widening tolerances. Preserve direct CALL/JMP, Jcc/JCXZ, LOOP, ordinary-I/O and word-transfer acceptance, external IRQ entry at 32/35 internal clocks and its former-charge rejection. Retain unchanged interval bounds where measured instructions are unaffected; preserve historical observations.
- [ ] Preserve startup/model and firmware policies, LCD/input/frame continuity, audio/PCM, DMA/Hyper Voice, SRAM/cartridge/internal EEPROM and RTC retention, browser save integrity, local data handling and ownership/provenance. Coordinator runs `python3 fixtures/build.py --check`, `python3 demo/build.py --check`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, and `git diff --check`. In `web`, run `npm run build:wasm`, `npm run build`, then complete `npm run test:browser` and `npm run test:compat` sequentially with `WS_PREVIEW_URL` pointing to an explicit local production preview.
- [ ] Record tested source/artifact identities, independent calculations, actual results, failures, corrections and unperformed checks. Coordinator reviews the final diff and evidence against every criterion and resolves blocking findings before merge. Mandatory acceptance uses automated native/browser tooling.

## Optional validation

Additional lawful software experiments, another browser engine, console measurements and human gameplay may supplement acceptance. These were unperformed during planning and are not merge prerequisites. Commercial-title compatibility and complete pipeline timing remain unestablished.

## Required post-merge verification

None.

## Specification reconciliation

This task was authored by AI under the agreed WonderSwan-family hardware goal.
Correct erroneous technical assumptions or acceptance criteria when primary hardware
specifications establish the correction. Update this Issue and record the original
assumption, corrected requirement, primary reference and rationale in the PR.
These technical corrections require neither human approval nor an independent AI
re-review. Preserve the agreed goal and relevant pre-merge acceptance; do not weaken
requirements merely to accommodate incomplete implementation or failing tests.

This autonomous campaign has no human-approval gate. Mandatory acceptance uses
automated native and production-browser tests on the emulator's supported model
and mode configurations. Physical-console measurements and human gameplay are
optional evidence and must remain explicitly unperformed unless actually available.
Do not invent device identities, real-device results or a requirement for human
confirmation. Resolve technical errors with recorded evidence and automated checks
through the existing Coordinator workflow.
